title: Ghosting Test: Are You Likely to Ghost? (15 Questions)
h1: Ghosting Test: Are You Likely to Ghost Someone?
searchIntent: am i likely to ghost someone

personalization.recoveryAfterSilence: Independent signal based on whether selected answers preserve a path back after delay, silence, or discomfort.
personalization.behaviorTags: Includes delay spiral, closure avoidance, slow fade, closeness retreat, overload, repair after silence, empathy, safety exit, and direct closure.

scoring.safetyRule: Safety-based blocking or ending contact is not scored like ordinary ghosting when contact is threatening, coercive, or repeatedly violates boundaries.

methodology.design: 15 scenario-based items distinguishing direct closure difficulty, communication overload, retreat after closeness, relational accountability, and recovery after silence.
methodology.limitations: The test cannot infer motive from silence alone and does not diagnose attachment style, personality disorder, or mental health conditions.
researchBackground: Ghosting research distinguishing unilateral unexplained communication cessation from mutual fading or explicit endings.
Research on communication overload as a contributor to ghosting and digital avoidance.
Research on attachment, conflict avoidance, and interpersonal disengagement as possible—not exclusive—contributors to ghosting behavior.
